Primary transcription only: Tsuchida's 1969 IPA record (column 'Taokas' here = Tsuchida 1982 Papora source 1-4) marks an acute accent on the final syllable of every polysyllabic form, usually with final vowel length (ŋinúː, moːróː, sɑrinɑ́ː, mɑsɑ́ː, mɑpúː, kɑpudúː, ɭimɑ́ː, tɑlɑkúː, ˀitɑ́n, mɑutúː, kuvíd, ɡyoːβéː, mɑdwɑ́ː, mɑitʃíː, bɑːtúː, ɭɑβíd, nɑkɑ́ː); the romanized 'Papora' column is unaccented except ˀitán, mantúː, maːráː, míaː. Wordlist-only evidence, consistent with final prominence in the last rememberers' citation forms; not a rule stated by any author.

sources.note: Nothing. Entirely segmental/lexical: loss of *k, loss of *-y, *s/*t merger in non-final position, *N/*n merger (Pap usu, Hoa usu; Pap parai, Hoa pira; Pap mapa, Hoa maθa; Pap s-m-ani, Hoa s-am-ani; Pap tubun, Hoa tuhun), Taokas-Babuza innovations, Thao's partial sharing, Pazih, tree, dispersal chronology; fn.4 Tsuchida's scepticism about Japanese-era transcription accuracy. No stress/accent/length/tone.

sources.citation: 土田滋 [Tsuchida, Shigeru]. 2002. 言語が消えるとき，何が起こるか (What happens in languages on the verge of extinction?). 地学雑誌 Journal of Geography (Chigaku Zasshi) 111(1):141-143. [地学クラブ講演要旨, lecture of 2001-12-20]
sources.note: First-hand remarks on the phonology of the last Papora/Taokas/Ketangalan rememberers: liquids r/l and b/m confused under Taiwanese influence; loss of word meanings; phrases remembered as unanalysed wholes; which semantic fields persist (Papora keeps 'liquor' across three generations). Nothing on stress, accent, length or tone.
sources.venue: 地学雑誌 Journal of Geography (Chigaku Zasshi)
